headline: Senators’ Linus Ullmark leaves game against Panthers
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Senators goalie Linus Ullmark left Wednesday's game against the Panthers after appearing to tweak something while making a save against Florida. The outlet's summary gives no word yet on the severity of the injury.

It matters because Ullmark has carried a lot of Ottawa's start. Goals saved above expected, which measures how many goals a goalie has stopped compared with what an average goalie would be expected to stop on the same shots, sits at 8.24 for him through 8 games so far this season, alongside a .945 save percentage. Last season he was at -13.3 over 49 games, so this is a sharp reversal, though the sample is small. His work accounts for most of the team's 2.9 goals saved above expected, and OTT's 7-3-0 record has come with a 51.2 percent share of expected goals, which is a measure of chance quality, so the team has been decent but not dominant. Without Ullmark's goaltending, that margin gets thinner. The data doesn't say who would step in or what the backup's numbers look like, so how Ottawa holds up depends on the injury's severity.
